title: Reception Administrator
description:
My specialist further educational client, based in Bolton town centre, is currently looking to recruit a Customer Service Assistant (Receptionist) on a temporary basis for 6-8 weeks. The role is to cover a period of leave and is an immediate start.

The successful candidate will have previous experience within a customer-facing, reception, or administrative role. You will be responsible for providing a professional front-of-house service, operating the main switchboard, welcoming visitors, and supporting the wider team with a variety of administrative duties.

Pay & Benefits:

Salary - £12.85 per hour

Working Hours - 36.25 hours per week, working either 8:30am to 4:45pm or 8:45am to 5:00pm

Potential assignment extension

Responsibilities:

Operate the switchboard, ensuring all internal and external calls are handled professionally and efficiently.

Welcome visitors to the site and direct them to the appropriate departments or meeting locations.

Provide travel information and arrange taxis for visitors and staff as required.

Undertake general reception duties and provide administrative support to the wider team.

Follow procedures for emergency situations, including fire alarms and the communication of urgent messages.

Maintain accurate visitor logs and car parking reservations.

Update internal databases, including staff extensions and room locations.

Carry out additional administrative duties as required.

Specification:

Previous experience within a reception, customer service, or front-of-house environment.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Professional and friendly telephone manner.

Competent IT user with experience using Microsoft Office, including Word and Excel.

Experience operating a switchboard would be advantageous.

A positive, proactive, and customer-focused approach.

If you have previous reception, customer service, or administrative experience and are looking for your next opportunity within a professional and supportive organisation, please do not hesitate to apply.

title: Part-time Administrator
description:
Administrator
- Job Type: Temporary, Part-time
- Location: Bolton, Lancashire, BL2 2 JW
- Duration: 3-4 months
- Pay: £13.74 per hour PAYE
- Working Hours: 3 days per week - all day Wednesday, Thursday and Friday (approx 22 hours 12 mins)

Bolton Council are excited to offer an opportunity for an experienced Administrator to join their Children's Social Care administration team at the Bolton Family. This role involves supporting the Child Protection Unit by scheduling Initial and Review Conferences. The role is key to ensuring the smooth running of our services and offers a variety of engaging tasks.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Preparing and sending out invite letters for Child Protection conferences, including verifying attendees and booking rooms.
- Re-arranging conferences and sending updates to attendees as required.
- Collating requests for reports, ensuring they are received in time for the relevant conference.
- Sending out notifications of discontinued or stepped-down plans.
- Checking GP involvement and updating records accordingly.
- Actioning Transfer-in requests.
- Monitoring the Child Protection Unit inbox and dealing with or signposting any queries as required.
- Adding and updating case notes to the relevant child's record on the Liquid Logic database.
- Joining a committed team that is proud of the service they deliver to help children, young people, and families achieve their potential.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Effective communication skills, capable of presenting information both verbally and in writing.
- Ability to work as part of a team and independently.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to plan, develop, and prioritise work.
- Proficiency in using computer software packages such as Word, Excel, and Outlook to produce accurate, well-presented documents.
- Excellent literacy skills to ensure correct information is collated and processed.

If you are interested in this role, please apply using your latest CV! and a Reed Consultant will be in touch!

title: Data Administrator
description:
Intelligence Data Administrator
- Job Type: Temporary, Full-time
- Location: Bolton, Lancashire, BL3 5 DT
- Pay: £13.74 per hour PAYE
- Duration: Until 30/01/2027
- Enhanced DBS Required.

Bolton Council are seeking a meticulous and detail-oriented Intelligence Data Administrator to manage and maintain intelligence data within their Intelligence Database (IDB) System. This role involves performing essential administrative duties and supporting operational teams with accurate information within Regulatory Services. The ideal candidate will possess strong data entry skills, an understanding of intelligence handling procedures, and the ability to maintain high levels of confidentiality and data security.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Provide general administrative support including filing, record keeping, and document management, ensuring sensitive information is handled with discretion and professionalism.
- Accurately input, update, and maintain intelligence data in the IDB system, adhering to security protocols. Verify and cross-check data sources to ensure accuracy and reliability.
- Handle verbal and written customer enquiries and complaints in accordance with Council policies and procedures, ensuring prompt and effective responses within service policy timelines.
- Organise and categorise intelligence reports for easy retrieval and analysis. Assist in generating reports and summaries from the IDB system as required, following strict confidentiality and data protection guidelines.
- Support and maintain the use of information systems and databases, recording and supplying relevant information as required.
- Support regulatory services with data requests and troubleshoot issues with the IDB system.
- Maintain logs and track intelligence submissions and updates.
- Work effectively with other team members and develop internal and external customer relationships to help support and improve the efficiency of the team.
- Undertake any other duties that are commensurate with the grading of the post.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Strong data entry skills and attention to detail.
- Understanding of intelligence handling procedures and data protection guidelines.
- Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.
- Experience in administrative support and document management.
- Proficiency in using information systems and databases.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to handle customer enquiries and complaints effectively.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

If you are interested in this role, please apply using your latest CV here!

title: Inventory Administrator
description:
Are you a highly organised administrator with excellent attention to detail and a passion for keeping operations running smoothly? If you're looking for a varied role where you can make a real impact within a growing business, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.

About the Company

Our client is a well-established and growing service-led organisation supporting customers across the UK. Operating within a fast-paced technical environment, they deliver a range of operational and field-based services and are recognised for their commitment to quality, customer service and continuous improvement. Due to ongoing growth, they are looking to strengthen their head office team with the addition of an Inventory Administrator.

About the Role

This is a varied administrative position that combines inventory management, customer support and operational coordination. Working closely with engineers, remote locations and internal teams, you will be responsible for maintaining accurate stock records, supporting day-to-day operations, and ensuring inventory processes are effectively managed.

Benefits
- Starting salary of £26,500
- Full-time, Mon-Fri
- 28 days holidays inclusive of bank holidays
- Company Pension
- Free car parking
- Regular social events
- Opportunity to join a growing and established business
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Career development and progression opportunities

Key Responsibilities
- Process and maintain accurate data across internal software systems
- Track and record all inbound and outbound stock movements
- Monitor, manage and report stock levels across engineers and remote depots
- Provide customer support via telephone and email
- Order and manage inventory, including spare parts and consumables
- Conduct regular stock checks and support inventory audits
- Produce and maintain administrative documentation and correspondence
- Assist with project coordination, resource allocation and engineer scheduling
- Ensure all records are maintained accurately and efficiently

Essential Skills & Experience
- Previous administration experience with a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail
- Proficient in Microsoft Word and Excel
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Confident communicator with a professional telephone manner
- Able to learn new systems and adapt to changing priorities
- Positive, proactive approach and ability to work effectively within a team

Desirable Skills
- Experience within customer service or customer support
- Previous experience in a technical, engineering or maintenance environment
- Knowledge of inventory management systems, such as Zoho Inventory
- Familiarity with Health & Safety documentation, including RAMS

If you're a detail-oriented administrator looking for a varied role within a growing business, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today to take the next step in your career and become part of a supportive team where your organisational skills and initiative will make a real difference.

title: Third Party Claims Handler
description:
Third Party Claims Handler

Location: Bolton
Salary: From £24,479 - £35,000 DOE
Hours: 35 hours per week, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Are you an experienced Motor Claims Handler with experience handling Third Party Vehicle Damage, Property Damage or Credit Hire claims?

We are currently recruiting for a Third Party Claims Handler to join a well-established and reputable insurance business based in Bolton.

Due to continued growth and internal promotions, this is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious claims professional looking to develop their career within a supportive and forward-thinking organisation.

The Role

As a Third Party Claims Handler, you will manage a portfolio of Third Party Vehicle Damage and Property Damage claims, ensuring cases are handled efficiently while delivering an excellent level of service to all parties involved.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing a portfolio of Third Party Motor and Property Damage claims.
- Prioritising your own workload and managing claims efficiently.
- Investigating claims and establishing liability.
- Handling more complex cases, including Liability and High Value claims.
- Liaising with solicitors, insurers, accident management companies and other third parties.
- Identifying and referring potentially fraudulent activity.
- Working closely with internal departments throughout the claims process.
- Delivering a consistently high level of customer service.

About You

We are looking for someone with previous experience within Motor Claims, Third Party Claims or Credit Hire who is looking for their next career opportunity.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience handling Third Party Motor claims and/or Credit Hire claims.
- Strong customer service and communication skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to build effective relationships with customers and third parties.
- Strong organisational and computer skills.
- The ability to manage and prioritise a busy workload.
- A CII qualification, or the willingness to work towards this.
- GCSE English and Maths at Grade C/4 or above, or equivalent.

Candidates with 2+ years of Motor Claims experience may be considered for the higher end of the salary range.

What's in it for you?

Alongside a competitive salary, you will receive an excellent benefits package, including:
- Increased holiday allowance with length of service.
- Your birthday off.
- Half-day off for seasonal shopping.
- Holiday sell scheme.
- Contributory pension scheme.
- Support with industry-relevant qualifications, including CII.
- Discounted sports and social activities.
- Free on-site parking.
- Casual dress code and branded clothing allocation.
- Cycle to Work scheme.
- Cash bonuses for going above and beyond.
- Trained Mental Health and First Aid staff on-site.
- Flexible working patterns available.
- Sociable Monday-Friday working hours.
- And much more!

If you're an experienced Motor Claims or Third Party Claims Handler looking for a new opportunity with genuine career progression and development, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today with your CV to be considered.

title: Casualty Litigated Claims Handler
description:
The Claims Handler will manage a caseload of EL/PL delegated authority fixed fee cases on behalf of a number of insurance clients, working in conjunction with a Technical Support Lawyer who will be involved in setting strategies and making liability decisions, as well as responsible for their technical development. The role requires a forensic and analytical approach to the issues together with experience and/or appreciation of the documents and evidence required in these types of cases.

The work type likely to feature in the case load are Pre-action disclosure files, Infant Approval Hearings and EL/PL files handled on a Delegated Authority basis. In addition the Assistant File Handler will support File Handlers on tasks within their caseloads.

Key Responsibilities

Duties will include the following (based on experience), but may not be limited to:
- Considering and responding to Applications for Pre-action disclosure
- Handling matters in accordance with client SLA's
- Instructing Counsel/advocate
- Reviewing evidence
- Legal Research
- Negotiations/ Drafting Payments into Court
- Dealing with routine correspondence
- Initial review and setting strategy for the management of the claim
- Reviewing matters throughout
- CRU
- Dealing with disclosure
- Reviewing evidence (including medical / personnel records)
- Conducting investigations with Insured's / obtaining witness statements
- Liaising with parties involved in claims including the insured, Claimant Solicitors and witnesses
- Instructing Counsel / Experts
- Attending conferences and Trials with Counsel and note taking
- Dealing with routine correspondence
- Reviewing quantum
- Drafting Tomlin Orders and Consent Orders
- Draft Cost schedules
- Dealing with general or straightforward queries
- Telephone chasing activities
- Filing out Allocation Questionnaires and witness summon
- Ensuring compliance with the SRA Standards & Regulations.

Working Hours

35 hours per week Monday - Friday 9am - 5pm with 1 unpaid hour for lunch. Primary location for this role is Parklands, Bolton Office

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Essential
- Self-confident with good telephone and communication skills with people at all levels inside and outside the business
- An ability to organise and prioritise tasks using initiative
- Calm under pressure with the ability to re-prioritise and delegate effectively when required
- An ability to maintain attention to detail when dealing with repetitive tasks
- Good Literacy and IT skills
- Good team worker with the flexibility to do what is required to get a result and ensure client service levels are met
- Ability to work effectively within the Keoghs Shared Behaviour framework
- Contributes actively to an environment in which colleagues work cooperatively with each other.
- Ability to meet performance targets
- Positive, confident and enthusiastic
- Excellent listening, verbal and written communication skills
- Good client care skills and evidence of working to client guidelines on a delegated basis
- Ability to prioritise work, keep to deadlines and work under pressure
- High level of analytical skills

Desirable
- Previous personal injury file handling experience
- Legal Education- ILEX, LPC or equivalent work experience
- Experience of handling a caseload of EL/PL files would be advantageous.
- Previous litigation experience is preferred
- Good advocacy skills

Values:

Our culture is focussed on making Keoghs sustainable and successful for our people and clients, with this our four values are at the heart of everything we do;

We are connected
We are Dynamic
We are Innovative
We succeed together

Benefits
- 25 days holiday per year which increases with level of service (opportunity to buy & sell 3 days)
- Family Cover Private Medical Insurance ( Bupa) - will automatically be at single cover level but can opt into family option within first month of joining.

title: Complaints Handler
description:
Complaints Handler. Bolton (BL2) £27,500. 25 days hol + BH's. 1 day per week WFH (12 month FTC )

A market leader in their sector, our client is looking for an experienced Complaints Handler to join the customer service department and be dedicated to taking ownership of issues and complaints and seeing them through to resolution. Duties will include;
- Taking details of the issue/complaint over the phone or via email, acknowledging receipt with the customer and talking them through the next steps
- Liaising with other departments, suppliers and other contractors involved to investigate the complaint
- Some queries will be quicker to resolve than others and may involve a simple refund of delivery charges. Others may be more complex and involve the return of faulty goods back to the manufacturer for further investigation which will take longer
- Keeping the customer updated at all stages of their case

To be successful, you will have a strong background in customer service and previous experience of handling complaints through to resolution. You will have excellent verbal and written communication skills and have the ability to remain calm and professional at all times.

Please forward your CV for immediate consideration, I look forward to hearing from you.

Please note that due to the high volume of applications we receive, only those successfully shortlisted for the role will be personally contacted.

Follow us on LinkedIn and Facebook for updates, recruitment information, new vacancies and more!

title: Receptionist Administrator
company: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
description: At GMMH we are investing significantly into our Community Mental Health provision. We are currently looking for an enthusiastic individual to join our Community Mental Health reception team. Applicants should be excellent communicators with good telephone skills and have the ability to deal with the general public on a daily basis and have a positive approach to customer care. The role will involve providing reception support to the clinical team within the Community Mental Health Teams. In addition it is a necessity that applicants have a good standard of IT skills and be able to work on their own initiative and as part of a team. Please note, this post is not eligible for sponsorship As a receptionist with the Community Mental Health Teams, you will be expected to provide a welcoming and professional first impression for our patients and Healthcare Professionals on arrival at the reception desk, whether this be front facing or via telephone, to ensure they receive an excellent customer service experience. You will be the first point of contact for anyone accessing the department therefore you must be able to deal professionally with a range of enquiries, in person, by phone or by email in an efficient, polite and courteous manner. The post holder will be responsible for providing clinic administration and reception support for the Bolton Community Mental Health Team. This will include receiving and greeting service users and their carers into clinic areas whilst recording the service users attendance and clinical outcome on the Electronic Patient Record (EPR), along with other administrative duties commensurate to the grade. The post holder will be interactive with the general public, nursing, medical staff, professionals and other Trust administrative and clerical staff and will ensure all reception processes are carried out in a timely and accurate manner to ensure an efficient reception and quality service to all users. The reception services opening hours are at present 09:00am to 17:00pm, Monday to Friday. A flexible approach to working is essential. In order to meet the needs of the Trust services you may be required, from time to time, to work outside of your normal area of work to cover absence/sickness. The Trust reserves the right to changes your normal area of work to any other location within the Bolton Trust services. Staff benefits Pay Enhancements 30% additional for Evenings (8pm onwards) and Saturdays and 60% additional for Sundays and Bank holidays. 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays rising to 29 after 5 years and 33 days after 10 years Excellent pension Cycle to work scheme Salary sacrifice car scheme Wellbeing programme Blue Light Card Discounts

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic GP Surgery Receptionist to join our busy and friendly practice team. The successful candidate will work Monday to Friday, 13:00pm to 6:30pm , and should be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the practice. As a key member of our reception team, you will be the first point of contact for patients, both face-to-face and over the telephone. You will provide a welcoming, professional and compassionate service while helping to ensure that patients receive timely and appropriate care. Previous experience working within a GP practice or general practice environment is essential, along with confidence using EMIS Web. Welcoming patients and visitors in a professional and compassionate manner. Handling telephone calls and patient queries efficiently, ensuring appropriate signposting. Booking, amending, and cancelling appointments via EMIS Web. Processing patient registrations, repeat prescription requests, and clinical correspondence. Scanning and accurately registering clinical documents onto patient records. Assisting with monitoring and recording data for QOF (Quality and Outcomes Framework) KPIs. Referring patients to the relevant specialties or external services as directed. Supporting clinicians and the wider team with administrative tasks. Ensuring confidentiality and compliance with NHS policies, GDPR, and safeguarding procedures. Greet and assist patients and visitors in a polite, professional, and compassionate manner. Answer and manage incoming telephone calls, dealing with patient queries and signposting appropriately. Book, amend, and cancel patient appointments using the practice clinical system (e.g., EMIS Web). Process new patient registrations, temporary residents, and patient record updates. Manage repeat prescription requests in line with practice protocols. Handle patient correspondence, referrals, and medical reports. Ensure the reception area is tidy, organised, and welcoming at all times. Scan, code, and file clinical documents into patient records accurately. Assist with monitoring and inputting data for QOF (Quality and Outcomes Framework) and other performance indicators. Prepare and send patient referrals to secondary care and community services. Support the management of recalls, long-term condition reviews, and screening programmes. Carry out administrative support for clinicians, nurses, and the management team. Maintain confidentiality and adhere to GDPR and NHS information governance policies. Contribute to maintaining practice policies, procedures, and quality standards.
